messages:
ashley: Hey team — hitting a reproducible hang with the Node/TS SDK on an edge runtime (Vercel). After our auth token rotates the ReadableStream never finishes and the lambda returns 502. SDK v1.2.3. Error in logs: ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE. Anyone seen this?

sara: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste minimal repro + network logs? Is this SSE or chunked ReadableStream?

ashley: It's the streaming chat path (SSE-like over fetch readable). Repro steps: deploy to vercel edge, call client.chat.stream with a long response, then trigger token rotation (our KMS rotates on refresh -> new token). After rotation the stream hangs. Quick snippet:

```
const res = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'redwood/gpt-xyz',
  stream: true,
  messages: [{role:'user', content:'long answer please'}]
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break; process.stdout.write(value);
}
```

logs: `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` then no `done`.

kyu: Interesting. Which fetch/runtime are you on? Vercel edge uses web fetch + ReadableStream. SDK v1.2.3 still has the retry wrapper that may re-attach a stream on 401 retry. That could cause the original reader to be left in a weird state.

jamal: Also check if your token swap code is calling client.setApiKey sync from another tick — if SDK retries and spawns a new request while the old stream hasn't been aborted you can get double-close behavior. We saw similar with older fetch polyfills.

ashley: We're not manually aborting. Token rotation is external: new token in env, we call a refresh endpoint and then subsequent requests pick it up. Happens automatically mid-stream when token expires (we saw 401 and then client retry).

kyu: Can you attach the raw headers for the failed stream response? Need to know if server sends `Connection: close` or `retry-after`. Also, does your retry logic re-fetch the same body? SDK retry should not attempt to stream-retry without aborting original.

ashley: Pasted headers from the failing request: `status: 401` then client retries and new request returns `200` but the ReadableStream stays attached to the first underlying body. Full sequence in logs: 401 -> SDK retry -> new 200 stream -> application reader still reading from initial body -> no done event.

sara: Ok this matches a known edge-case. Short-term workaround: pin server-side token rotation to avoid mid-stream changes or disable automatic SDK retry for streaming calls. Example: set `{retry: {maxRetries:0}}` for stream calls.

kyu: Longer term fix: we should ensure the SDK aborts the in-flight stream when a retry is triggered for auth. I'll open a small runtime patch: when status is 401 and we decide to retry, call controller.abort() on the reader's underlying stream before spawning a new fetch. That should surface done.

jamal: Adding: on edge runtimes the ReadableStream CAN end up detached if the underlying body is replaced without proper cancel. Also watch for `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` which indicates the node-side stream closed unexpectedly — we need to propagate that as done.

devx-bot: Sentry summary: 8 alerts last 24h for ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE from sdk@1.2.3 on vercel-edge (customer: acme).

sara: Ashley — can you try the workaround and report back? Commands: `npm i @redwood/sdk@canary` or set `client.config.retry.maxRetries = 0` for streaming. If you can share a small repro gist I can run on our side. :thumbsup:

ashley: Trying `client.config.retry.maxRetries = 0` now. Will re-deploy and report in ~10m. Thanks all. :pray:

kyu: I'll draft a fix for the retry-abort flow and link a PR to this thread once opened.

sara: Filing internal ticket `INF-4321` to track customer hit + patch; labeling P0 for v1.2.x users.

ashley: Update: disabling retries for stream fixed it in our staging. No more hang.

sara: Great, leaving this open until kyu's patch lands. Thanks! :tada:
